note: Credit and provenance for every asset under ui/board_v2/. Kept in the same machine-readable shape as ui/assets/attribution.json and ui/assets-gothic/attribution.json, so one reader answers the licence question for any tree in this repository.
reproducibility: Two kinds of file live here and they are not equally recoverable. SCRIPT OUTPUT is regenerable: the recipe is recorded per file and was checked rather than quoted, so re-running it reproduces the committed pixels. MODEL OUTPUT is not, because the same prompt does not produce the same picture twice -- which is why every generated master is committed and kept forever, and why anything derived from one records the master it came from.

project-generated.name: Generated by a script in this repository. Nothing traced, photographed or diffused, and no model-generated content is in the file, so there is no upstream licence to honour and nothing to attribute. Where the design was arrived at with an assistant, the file's `design` note says so -- a record of how the decisions were reached, not a rights claim.

openai-generated.name: OpenAI-generated output; rights assigned to the user under the OpenAI Europe Terms of Use. Not CC0, public domain or royalty-free stock

layout_lab/assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.design: Proportions and palette arrived at by iteration in project sessions with Claude (Anthropic): 1.887 chosen over the builder's default 1.778, the 32 degree elevation that follows from it, and the recolour from the builder's parchment into slate. The file itself is deterministic output of the builder and contains no model-generated content -- no raster data, nothing traced or diffused, only computed vector geometry.
layout_lab/assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.role: the drawing the layout lab composes the module around. generate_layout_lab.py reads it as bytes, recolours it to slate at build time, and refuses any aspect more than 0.0005 from the design ratio.
layout_lab/assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.recipe: python3 tools/ui_debug/build_duty_wheel_v2.py --aspect 1.887 --out duty_wheel_v2_1887_layout.json, then render with tools.ui_debug.render_duty_wheel_v2.render_duty_wheel_v2_svg(lay, standalone=True) from tools/ui_debug/duty_wheel_v2_1887_layout.json. See ui/board_v2/layout_lab/README.md for the exact snippet.

duty_actions/clerical/gain_piety/clerica.notes: NOT PRODUCED BY tools/duty_art/crop_duty_master.py, and the entry deliberately carries no reproducibleBy for that reason. The script anchors both crops flush to the master's edges; this pair is inset 3 px at each side, symmetrically, and is RGB where the script writes RGBA. The geometry above is exact and was checked, so the pair is reproducible in principle -- but not by the tool as it stands, and saying otherwise would give a false recipe. OPEN QUESTION: whether the 3 px inset is deliberate, such as trimming a dirty generated edge, or incidental. If deliberate the script wants an inset option and this pair should go under the same pixel-for-pixel guard as v01; if not, the pair should be re-cut flush.

defaultProvenance: UNLESS AN ENTRY SAYS OTHERWISE, AN IMAGE IN THIS TREE WAS GENERATED WITH ChatGPT (OpenAI) and carries the openai-generated licence. That is the project's stated default for artwork, not a guess made per file: anything with a different origin -- a third-party icon, a hand-drawn asset, deterministic script output -- has to say so in its own entry, because the default would otherwise quietly mislabel it. A new image added here with no entry at all is a gap, not an implicit default; tests/layout_lab/test_board_v2_attribution.py fails on one.
